description: A user can download any cover letter directly as a PDF file and as a Word (.docx) file, and can create a translated copy of a letter by clicking one of four language flags, the same flags as the grammar checker.

userStories.title: A cover letter downloads as a real PDF file
userStories.description: As a user, I want to download my cover letter as a PDF file in one click, so that I can attach it to an application without going through printing.
acceptanceCriteria: "Télécharger PDF" in the list ⋮ menu, and a PDF button in the editor, download a `.pdf` file named after the letter's title. No print dialog opens.
The file is a real PDF with extractable text, not a picture of the page.
It contains every non-empty part of the letter, in order: sender; date; recipient and company block; subject; greeting; opening; each body paragraph; closing; sign-off; signature name.
Its layout matches today's PDF export of the same letter: the same template and the same section order. Fonts may be embedded rather than rasterized.
Rich text in the paragraphs (bold, italic, lists) keeps its meaning.
A long letter flows onto a second page without clipping.
From the editor, the PDF reflects the saved letter. If there are unsaved changes, the user is told to save first; the download does not silently save.
Another user's letter id is refused, with no file.
A generation failure shows a localized error, and no broken file is downloaded.

FR-1: The PDF is generated server-side, reusing the resume PDF infrastructure (`src/lib/pdf/browser.ts`): the same browser launch, concurrency limit and time limit. The HTML source is the existing `buildCoverLetterPdfHtml`, so there is no second letter layout.
FR-2: The DOCX is generated server-side with the `docx` library already in the project. There is no new dependency.
FR-3: Download and translate routes are authenticated. They read the letter with the user's session and an explicit `user_id` check.
FR-4: The flags exist once, in a shared component used by both the grammar checker and the cover-letter editor.
FR-5: Translation reuses the existing AI translation route or its core, with its fr/en/de/it validation and the AI rate limit. The guarded AI test stub covers it in e2e.
FR-6: No schema migration and no new dependency.
FR-7: New UI strings exist, non-empty, in fr, en, de and it (`src/locales/locale-parity.test.ts`).
Regression constraint: The grammar checker's language selection behaves and looks as before.
Regression constraint: The cover-letter editor's existing sections, autosave and AI generation modal are unchanged. The specs `cover-letter-editor-i18n` and `cover-letter-editor-spacing` stay green.
Regression constraint: Resume PDF and DOCX exports are unchanged. Parity stays NEW 0 / KNOWN 3, and the resume PDF/DOCX e2e specs stay green.
Regression constraint: `e2e/cover-letter-pdf-export.spec.ts` is updated to the new direct PDF, and its content assertions still pass.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline, plus `pnpm test:parity`.
Verification: Unit tests: DOCX content and order; ownership; error paths; the translation copy (fields kept, fields translated, sanitized, nothing created on failure).

Verification: e2e in fr and de, for downloads from the list and from the editor: PDF: magic bytes, extractable text containing every part in order; DOCX: `word/document.xml` containing every part in order; translate by flag: the new letter opens in the target language, and the original is unchanged.
Verification: `export-validation` on generated PDF and DOCX artifacts of a full letter and a long letter, including the comparison with today's PDF for the same letter.
Verification: `visual-regression` on the grammar checker's flags, before and after.
Verification: `security-review` on the routes and the server-side render.
Verification: `ui-expert` on the menu, the editor buttons and the flags, in fr and de at 1440 and 375.
Verification: `code-reviewer`.
FAIL condition: The PDF download opens a print dialog, or produces an image-only PDF.
FAIL condition: Any non-empty part of the letter is missing from the PDF or the DOCX.
FAIL condition: The flags differ from the grammar checker's, or the grammar checker's flags change.
FAIL condition: Translation modifies the original letter or re-points the application to the copy.
FAIL condition: A failed translation creates a letter.
FAIL condition: A user can download or translate another user's letter.
BLOCKER condition: The server-side PDF cannot reuse the resume PDF browser setup on the deployment target. Report it; the owner decides.
BLOCKER condition: A Word rendering requirement needs a renderer that isn't available. Content checks still run, and visual Word parity is reported as BLOCKED.

Out of scope: The letter template's English date and "Re: Application for …" line. This is a separate PRD candidate recorded by cover-letter-from-job; the PDF and Word keep whatever the template prints today.
Out of scope: New cover-letter templates or layout changes.
Out of scope: Translating in place, or translating a letter not yet saved.
Out of scope: Translating CVs, or changing the resume translate chips.
Out of scope: Exporting from the public cover-letter generator tool.
Out of scope: Changing the AI provider, model or rate limits.

userStories.title: A letter can be translated by flag into a new copy
userStories.description: As a user, I want to click a flag to get my letter in another language, so that I can apply in that language without rewriting it.
acceptanceCriteria: The editor shows four flags (EN, FR, DE, IT). They are drawn by the same SVGs as the grammar checker, from one shared component.
The grammar checker's flags look identical before and after, by a pixel comparison of the checker's language selector.
Each flag has an accessible name in the page language (e.g. "Traduire en allemand"), works with the keyboard, and shows a localized busy state while translating.

Clicking a flag creates a new letter and opens it. The new letter: is titled "<original title> (DE)" (or EN/FR/IT); has the greeting, opening, body paragraphs, closing and sign-off translated into that language, through the existing AI translation path; keeps the recipient, company, sender name, template, `resume_id` and `job_application_id`.
The original letter is unchanged, and the application's `cover_letter_id` still points to the original.
If the translation fails or is rate-limited, a localized error is shown and no letter is created.
The translated text is untrusted AI output. It is sanitized with the same rules as cover-letter-from-job before storage, and paragraphs keep their bold, italic and list meaning.
Translating another user's letter is refused.
